The confirmed metadata supplies an explicit date filter on the 'date' column for 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31, so the same regression is retained with that filter applied.

interpretation.summary: A simple ordinary least squares linear regression was performed with x as the predictor and y as the outcome, restricted to the calendar-year date filter, using complete cases only. The estimated slope of y on x was 1.4421, meaning y is estimated to change by that amount per one-unit increase in x, with a ninety-five percent confidence interval from 1.0622 to 1.8219. The associated p-value was 1.8009e-08, based on 30 observations. The slope direction is positive, indicating that higher x values correspond to higher y values on average within this sample. Because the p-value is below the five percent threshold, the evidence for a nonzero linear association is classified as evidence. This is an associational estimate from an observational design and does not imply that changes in x cause changes in y. The confidence interval describes estimation uncertainty under the model assumptions; it does not describe prediction intervals for individual observations. Warnings carried forward include a potential influential observations diagnostic, a heteroscedasticity diagnostic warning that the ordinary slope p-value and interval may be unreliable, and the fact that the linear mean model, independence, and constant error variance are not established by diagnostics. No observations were dropped beyond complete-case handling, and no automatic estimator change was applied.
limitations: This analysis does not establish causality.
The linear regression assumes a linear mean relationship, independent observations, and constant error variance; these assumptions were not established by the diagnostics.
A heteroscedasticity diagnostic warning was present, so the ordinary slope p-value and confidence interval may be unreliable.
A potential influential observations diagnostic was flagged; no observations were removed automatically, so results may be sensitive to those points.
The confidence interval reflects estimation uncertainty under the model and does not cover prediction of individual outcomes.
The analysis used complete cases only, so results may differ if missing data are not missing completely at random.
The estimate is associational and should not be interpreted as a causal effect of x on y.
No practical or clinical importance can be judged without additional context and units.
